sentences.en: So, but it's a nice story.

sentences.zh: 当然，那里有港口，壮观的港口。

sentences.zh: 这正是他们在此定居的原因。

sentences.en: But the other thing is that it is perfectly situated to dominate two alternative trade routes.
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是，它的地理位置极其优越，可以控制两条不同的贸易路线。

sentences.en: So one, obviously from Phoenicia in the east, right the way up to Spain in the west, but also just as crucially north-south.

sentences.en: So you've got Sicily, very accessible just across the sea.
sentences.zh: 比如西西里岛，隔海相望，非常容易到达。

sentences.en: Oh, right.

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Or the Numidians, who we also mentioned.
sentences.zh: 或者我们之前提到过的努米底亚人。

sentences.en: So I think to begin with, it's primarily a trading city.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为一开始，它主要是一个贸易城市。

sentences.en: And so this is why Carthage itself, of course, is a colonial settlement, but they then start going out and planting settlements

sentences.en: And these are not towns.
sentences.zh: 这些还算不上城镇。

sentences.en: These are just kind of trading posts.
sentences.zh: 这只是一种贸易前哨站。

sentences.en: So rather like the settlements that say the Venetians would have put up later or the Portuguese in Africa.
sentences.zh: 很像威尼斯人后来建立的定居点，或者葡萄牙人在非洲建立的定居点。

sentences.en: So sort of forts and markets, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是堡垒和市场。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 就像葡萄牙人的定居点一样，其背后有一种暴力的支撑。

sentences.en: So it's kind of bad news for the locals, really.
sentences.zh: 所以对当地人来说，这真算不上什么好消息。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 因此，到了公元前6世纪，迦太基相对于腓尼基而言不再是殖民地了。

sentences.en: And in part, that's because back in Phoenicia, the Babylonians have conquered Tyre.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，远在腓尼基的巴比伦人征服了提尔。

sentences.zh: 所以经历了一场长达13年的围城战。

sentences.en: And so basically the Tyrean economy implodes.

sentences.en: Inflation, Tom.

sentences.en: So again, a bit like America and Britain, I guess.

sentences.en: But it's imperialism.

sentences.zh: 据说他在西西里岛和撒丁岛进行了激烈的军事行动。

sentences.en: And his exploits seem to be slightly exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 他的功绩似乎被略微夸大了。

sentences.en: But it does suggest that the Greeks are starting to arrive on the scene now.
sentences.zh: 但这确实表明希腊人开始登上历史舞台了。

sentences.zh: 所以迦太基人曾经一帆风顺，但现在希腊人出现了，开始在西西里、撒丁岛、高卢南部和西班牙争夺资源。

sentences.zh: 因此，此时的地中海没有所谓的超级大国。

sentences.zh: 一切都还是未知数，对吧？

sentences.en: And has been accustomed to having its own way on the kind of the trade front for a fair while.

sentences.zh: 所以这些城市都建立在极其适合建城的地方。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 所以它现在不叫齐兹真是太遗憾了。

sentences.en: And a bit like Tyre, it's on an island.
sentences.zh: 和提尔有点像，它坐落在一个岛上。

sentences.zh: 所以考古学家们得以对它进行研究。

sentences.zh: 他们知道它在公元前6世纪是什么样子的。

sentences.zh: 但腓尼基人控制着染料市场。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: So by 600, you are getting cities that are almost going toe to toe with the Phoenicians.

sentences.zh: 转向一种更具西班牙风格的方法。

sentences.en: Or dare I say a Roman one.
sentences.zh: 或者我敢说罗马式的方法。

sentences.en: So those Venetian settlements in the west of Sicily, so Panormus and Mocia, for instance, by the fourth century, they have basically been absorbed into a Carthaginian empire.
sentences.zh: 因此，西西里岛西部的那些威尼斯定居点，例如帕诺尔穆斯和莫蒂亚，到公元前四世纪时，基本上已经被并入迦太基帝国。

sentences.en: And at the same time, Carthage is also planting colonies in Sicily of its own directly to maintain its control.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，迦太基也在西西里岛直接建立自己的殖民地，以维持其控制。

sentences.en: Because of course, you've got Carthage on the African side of that strait and you've got Sicily, the western side of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，海峡的非洲一侧有迦太基，而西西里岛则是西侧。

sentences.en: Carthage absolutely needs to control those seas because without it, you know, its trade will be throttled.
sentences.zh: 迦太基绝对需要控制这些海域，因为没有它，你知道的，它的贸易将被扼杀。

sentences.en: So the major city that it founds in this period is what's now Marsala, as in the wine, Nelson's favourite wine, but was known by the Romans as Lilibaeum.
sentences.zh: 因此，它在此期间建立的主要城市就是现在的马尔萨拉，正如那种酒，纳尔逊最爱的酒，但在当时被罗马人称为利利巴尤姆。

sentences.en: And this is founded in 397 after the Syracusans had captured and obliterated Mocia, the foul smelling city on the island with its garum factory.
sentences.zh: 这座城市建于公元前397年，此前叙拉古人攻占并彻底摧毁了莫蒂亚，那个岛上臭气熏天、拥有鱼露工厂的城市。

sentences.en: And Lilibaeum is founded to be a kind of, you know, a sanctuary for people who had fled Mocia.
sentences.zh: 利利巴尤姆的建立是为了成为逃离莫蒂亚的人们的避难所。

sentences.en: But also it's settled by lots and lots of Carthaginian colonists.
sentences.zh: 但同时它也居住了大量来自迦太基的殖民者。

sentences.en: And it's basically the westernmost point of Sicily.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是西西里岛的最西端。

sentences.en: And it has massive walls, so kind of 20 feet, has a great big ditch.
sentences.zh: 它拥有巨大的城墙，大约20英尺高，还有一条很大的壕沟。

sentences.en: It's built to be completely impregnable.
sentences.zh: 它的建造旨在完全不可攻破。

sentences.en: And this idea of a Carthaginian empire that is simultaneously Phoenician, I think is exemplified by the fact that this is the point when the
sentences.zh: 这种既是迦太基又是腓尼基的帝国理念，我认为可以通过一个事实来例证，即正是在这个时候，

sentences.en: Carthaginians introduce their coinage with the palm tree on it.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人引入了印有棕榈树图案的硬币。

sentences.en: And the Greek word for palm tree is phoenix.
sentences.zh: 而希腊语中棕榈树的单词是菲尼克斯。

sentences.en: And so there's a kind of allusion there to the idea of the Phoenicians.
sentences.zh: 因此这里有一种对腓尼基人概念的暗指。

sentences.en: So they're still, even at this late stage, very much into the kind of Phoenician heritage.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在这个晚期阶段，他们仍然非常沉浸在腓尼基人的传统中。

sentences.en: They are, because it provides a way of allowing what had previously been independent Phoenician settlements to feel that they have a kind of stake in what effectively is becoming
sentences.zh: 他们确实如此，因为这提供了一种方式，让先前独立的腓尼基定居点觉得它们对实际上正在变成的东西有一种投入感

sentences.en: a Carthaginian empire.
sentences.zh: 一个迦太基帝国。

sentences.en: And if they capture Greek cities, so they capture Salinas, for instance, on the south coast, there's always been a kind of thorn in the Carthaginian side.
sentences.zh: 如果他们攻占希腊城市，比如南海岸的塞利努斯，那里一直是迦太基人的心头大患。

sentences.en: They capture that and they plant a Phoenician garrison on the Acropolis and other Greek cities are made tributary.
sentences.zh: 他们攻占了那里，并在卫城驻扎了腓尼基卫戍部队，其他希腊城市则沦为朝贡国。

sentences.en: So that basically in this period, the fact that Carthage rules the western half of Sicily
sentences.zh: 所以基本上在这段时期，迦太基统治着西西里岛西部这一事实

sentences.en: is being established by treaties that are being signed with, you know, Syracuse and with other
sentences.zh: 是通过与锡拉库扎以及东部的其他

sentences.en: Greek cities in the eaSt. And so we're now into the age of Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 希腊城市签署条约来确立的。现在我们进入了亚历山大大帝的时代。

sentences.en: And so I think that by this point, Carthage is kind of becoming an empire in a way that would be recognisable, say, to Alexander.
sentences.zh: 因此我认为，到了这个时候，迦太基正在以一种亚历山大所能理解的方式崛起为帝国。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Tom Alexander obviously never did conquer Carthage, but he was said to have thought about it.
sentences.zh: 所以汤姆，亚历山大显然从未征服过迦太基，但据说他考虑过这件事。

sentences.en: And presumably that reflects a wider ambition among sort of
sentences.zh: 这大概反映了某种更广泛的雄心，即

sentences.en: Greek warlords, as it were.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上的希腊军阀的雄心。

sentences.en: They think, you know, let's bring Carthage down.
sentences.zh: 他们会想，你知道的，让我们把迦太基摧毁吧。

sentences.en: Carthage is a prize worth taking.
sentences.zh: 迦太基是一个值得拿下的战利品。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think obviously what Alexander's example does is give to other Greeks the notion
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我认为很明显，亚历山大的榜样给其他希腊人灌输了一种观念

sentences.en: that going off and conquering great empires, you know, what a tremendous thing to do.
sentences.zh: 即出征并征服伟大的帝国，这是一件多么了不起的事情。

sentences.en: And Carthage is a kind of obvious one.
sentences.zh: 而迦太基就是一个显而易见的目标。

sentences.en: And so say in Syracuse, you know, as we've said, the Syracuse are endlessly going to war with Carthage, but there is this sense that it's kind
sentences.zh: 所以在锡拉库扎，正如我们所说，锡拉库扎人一直在与迦太基交战，但人们有一种感觉，这就

sentences.en: of like a sport where, you know, it's governed by rules.
sentences.zh: 像是一场体育运动，你知道的，它受规则制约。

sentences.en: Neither one is trying to knock the other one out.
sentences.zh: 双方都没有试图把对方彻底击倒。

sentences.en: But in the wake of Alexander and his successes, you have this guy called Agathocles.
sentences.zh: 但在亚历山大及其成功之后，出现了一个名叫阿加托克利斯的人。

sentences.en: He was actually a very humble stock.
sentences.zh: 他实际上出身非常卑微。

sentences.en: He's a kind of a son of a potter, but he rises to become the tyrant of Syracuse.
sentences.zh: 他有点像个陶器的儿子，但最终崛起成为了锡拉库扎的僭主。

sentences.en: And he actually ends up invading Africa.
sentences.zh: 他甚至最终入侵了非洲。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, this is the first time that a Greek army has landed in Africa.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是希腊军队第一次在非洲登陆。

sentences.en: And at one point it looks as though Carthage is going to fall to Agathocles.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，迦太基似乎要败在阿加托克利斯手下了。

sentences.en: And if that had happened, then obviously that would have been a feat comparable to Alexander overthrowing Persia.
sentences.zh: 如果真的发生了，那显然将是一个堪比亚历山大推翻波斯的壮举。

sentences.en: And we're told that Carthage is reduced to such desperate straits by this invasion that they immolate 500 of the children of the Carthaginian elite.
sentences.zh: 据说迦太基人被这次入侵逼到了绝境，他们将迦太基精英阶层的500名儿童作为祭品火祭。

sentences.en: In desperation.
sentences.zh: 在绝望之中。

sentences.en: In desperation.
sentences.zh: 在绝望之中。

sentences.en: In the event it all goes wrong, there's a kind of uprising back in Syracuse and
sentences.zh: 结果这一切都搞砸了，锡拉库扎爆发了一场某种形式的起义，

sentences.en: Agathocles has to go back home, Scarpa's back.
sentences.zh: 阿加托克利斯不得不回国，溜回了家。

sentences.en: And the Carthaginians sign a treaty with the Agathocles, which is, I mean, it's pretty tough on them.
sentences.zh: 迦太基人与阿加托克利斯签署了一项条约，我的意思是，这对他们来说相当苛刻。

sentences.en: They have to pay a large indemnity, but they survive.
sentences.zh: 他们必须支付巨额赔款，但他们活了下来。

sentences.en: And within a few decades, they are back as prosperous, as intimidating as ever.
sentences.zh: 短短几十年内，他们就恢复了昔日的繁荣与威严。

sentences.en: And so Carthage has survived where Persia didn't.
sentences.zh: 因此，波斯灭亡了，而迦太基幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Carthage has held off, you know, the Greek adventurer trying to overthrow it.
sentences.zh: 迦太基抵挡住了试图推翻它的希腊冒险家。

sentences.en: And I think that that's tribute to the fact that it's just a very, very formidable power.
sentences.zh: 我认为这归功于它是一个非常、非常强大的强权。

sentences.en: I mean, probably we arrive at the dawning of the third century BC.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们大概来到了公元前三世纪的黎明。

sentences.en: It's clearly the most formidable power in the Western Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 它显然是西地中海最强大的强权。

sentences.en: The comparison that we mentioned in the last episode, we talked about how after the French
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中提到过这样一个对比，我们谈到在法国大革命之后

sentences.en: Revolution, during the kind of French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars, the French would say, well, we are the land power, we are Rome, and Britain is Carthage.
sentences.zh: 在法国大革命和拿破仑战争期间，法国人会说，我们是陆地强权，我们就是罗马，而英国就是迦太基。

sentences.en: You know, sort of only interested in money and navies.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，只对金钱和海军感兴趣。

sentences.en: Is Carthage still similar?
sentences.zh: 迦太基还是这样吗？

sentences.en: So you said that Carthage was becoming more of a kind of land empire with bases and forts and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才说，迦太基正变得越来越像一个拥有基地、要塞之类设施的陆地帝国。

sentences.en: But is it still very, very reliant on its navy rather than its army?
sentences.zh: 但它是否仍然非常、非常依赖海军而不是陆军？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, to pursue the comparison with Britain, of course, I mean, the British are not averse to conquering territory, but they are tending to do it because they need
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，如果继续与英国进行类比，当然，英国人并不排斥征服领土，但他们往往这样做是因为他们需要

sentences.en: naval bases.
sentences.zh: 海军基地。

sentences.en: And then to maintain their naval bases, they need to control the hinterland and they need to keep the French out or whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后为了维持海军基地，他们需要控制腹地，需要把法国人挡在外面等等。

sentences.en: And I think it's rather similar to that.
sentences.zh: 我想这挺类似的。

sentences.en: The Carthaginians are not necessarily interested in territory for its own sake, but they are interested absolutely
sentences.zh: 迦太基人对领土本身不一定感兴趣，但他们绝对

sentences.en: in maintaining their control of Western Sicily, because otherwise they'll lose control of the
sentences.zh: 有兴趣保持对西西里岛西部的控制，因为否则他们就会失去对

sentences.en: Straits.
sentences.zh: 海峡的控制。

sentences.en: They want to keep control of Sardinia.
sentences.zh: 他们希望保持对萨丁尼亚的控制。

sentences.en: They want to keep control of Southern Spain, because without that, you know, they won't be able to maintain the source of their wealth, which is trade.
sentences.zh: 他们希望保持对西班牙南部的控制，因为如果没有这些，你知道的，他们就无法维持财富的来源，也就是贸易。

sentences.en: But that is why the French do compare Britain in the Napoleonic Wars to Carthage.
sentences.zh: 但这就是为什么法国人在拿破仑战争中把英国比作迦太基。

sentences.en: And actually, the weird thing is that all the places that you've mentioned, they're the sort of places, I mean, you said about Nelson liking that wine.
sentences.zh: 事实上，奇怪的是，你提到的所有地方，都是那种地方，我是说你提过纳尔逊喜欢那种酒。

sentences.en: They're the places that he's always visiting.
sentences.zh: 那些地方就是他经常造访的地方。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: For the same reason.
sentences.zh: 出于同样的原因。

sentences.en: So the Carthaginians are interested in the same harbours that the British are interested in the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 所以迦太基人感兴趣的港口，和18世纪英国人感兴趣的港口是一样的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because if you want a blue water empire, you have to have a bit of territorial control.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你想要一个蓝水帝国，你就必须具备一定的领土控制权。

sentences.en: I mean, by this point, I realised that we haven't actually described what Carthage looks like in its heyday.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，到了这个时候，我意识到我们还没真正描述过迦太基在其全盛时期的样子。

sentences.en: It is a very, very impressive city, because it's a very wealthy city.
sentences.zh: 这是一座非常、非常令人印象深刻的城市，因为它非常富有。

sentences.en: So you've still got, you know, the Bersa, this Acropolis, which is the kind of the old town.
sentences.zh: 所以你依然拥有伯萨，这个作为老城的卫城。

sentences.en: The old city is counterpointed by a kind of grid system.
sentences.zh: 古老的城市与某种网格系统相映成趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's kind of cutting edge design of the same kind that you have in Alexandria.
sentences.zh: 那是尖端的设计，和你在亚历山大港看到的是同一种。

sentences.en: And if you imagine kind of the Acropolis, the Bersa and slopes running down to the sea, the streets look like a kind of fan running down to the shoreline.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下卫城伯萨和通往大海的山坡，街道看起来就像一把扇子延伸到海岸线。

sentences.en: Further from the old centre of the city, you have kind of beautiful villas.
sentences.zh: 离城市旧中心较远的地方，你会看到美丽的别墅。

sentences.en: You have docks.
sentences.zh: 你有船坞。

sentences.en: You have harbours.
sentences.zh: 你有港口。

sentences.en: You have massive arsenals.
sentences.zh: 你有巨大的军械库。

sentences.en: You have teeming industrial zones.
sentences.zh: 你有熙熙攘攘的工业区。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You have the Tophet, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然还有托斐特圣域。

sentences.en: You have cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 你有墓地。

sentences.en: Temples, Tom.
sentences.zh: 神庙，汤姆。

sentences.en: Beautiful temples.
sentences.zh: 美丽的神庙。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Particularly to Balhamon, the great patron, and Tanit, his partner.
sentences.zh: 特别是献给伟大的主神巴力哈蒙和他的伴侣塔尼特。

sentences.en: These are the great patrons of Carthage.
sentences.zh: 这些是迦太基的伟大主神。

sentences.en: But you also have massive bristling walls, and these extend more than 18 miles around the limits of the city.
sentences.zh: 但你也有坚固的、密密麻麻的城墙，它们沿着城市边缘绵延18英里以上。

sentences.en: And these are what had seen Agathocles of.
sentences.zh: 这就是让阿加托克利斯束手无策的东西。

sentences.en: He just, you know, he couldn't break through.
sentences.zh: 他就是，你知道的，他无法突破。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you'd look at Carthage at the beginning of the third century BC, and you'd say, you know, she is absolutely secure.
sentences.zh: 如果你在公元前三世纪初看着迦太基，你会说，你知道的，她是绝对安全的。

sentences.en: No one can possibly rival her.
sentences.zh: 没有人能与她匹敌。

sentences.en: Her only conceivable rival,
sentences.zh: 她唯一可能存在的对手

sentences.en: Syracuse, has had a crack and has dismally failed.
sentences.zh: 锡拉库扎，已经尝试过了却惨遭失败。

sentences.en: You know, she's going to last forever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她将永远存在下去。

sentences.en: Hmm.

sentences.zh: 我是说，谁能与她匹敌？

sentences.zh: 好吧，我们将在下一集中揭晓，届时我们将探讨罗马的崛起。

sentences.zh: 天哪，多么有戏剧性。

sentences.zh: 你现在就可以收听。
